method: per-node attribute comparison using the evaluator's own _match_nodes / norm_role / norm_system / _data_recall, with each mismatch classified by reading the stakeholder Observations + conversation.

actor.note: All 10 = agent actor 'I (the stakeholder)' vs GT 'sales'. Stakeholder is the sales employee and says 'I ...'. norm_role lacks first-person/self-reference aliases (has 'interviewee'/'you'/'yourself' but not 'i'/'me'/'stakeholder'). Runs 01/03/04 wrote 'Interviewee' (matches); runs 00/02 wrote 'I (the stakeholder)' (misses).

system.note: A: run_01 send step (stakeholder said 'by email', agent left system=None) + run_01 month-end (stakeholder said 'as an Excel file', agent left system=None). D: approval node system='quoting' left None in runs 01/02/03/04 because the stakeholder never states the approval happens in the quoting system.

reads.note: B: read 'quote' (GT) vs agent 'quotation'/'quotation information' - token matcher treats quote/quotation as different (not a substring; no stem). C: send node reads empty (stakeholder only says 'send it'). D: approval node reads empty (manager-reviewing-the-quote is never stated).

writes.note: B: create-quotation write 'quote' (GT) vs 'quotation' (agent), 5/5. C: GT models write artifacts (request / sent_quote / approval) that the stakeholder does not verbalize as outputs (r record request, sq send by email, ap needs approval); agent records no write. A: month-end write 'excel_summary' empty in runs 02/04 although the stakeholder explicitly says 'send a summary ... as an Excel file'.

recurring_patterns.fix: deterministic quote<->quotation normalization / small synonym map in _data_recall
add first-person / self-reference actor aliases (i/me/stakeholder/the interviewee) since the stakeholder IS the actor; also encourage cleaner role labels
stakeholder known_info never states the approval happens in the quoting system; either add it to the scenario or drop ap.system from GT (GT/scenario consistency)

recurring_patterns.pattern: writes request / sent_quote / approval not recorded by agent
recurring_patterns.fix: GT models explicit write artifacts the stakeholder does not verbalize as outputs; review GT write granularity or add to scenario disclosure
manager-reviews-the-quote is never stated; GT/scenario consistency

dominant_causes: evaluator too strict on synonymous data wording (quote vs quotation) and first-person actor labeling
Ground Truth models write/read data artifacts the stakeholder does not verbalize
a few GT attributes (approval system/read) not present in the stakeholder known_info
conclusion.takeaway: The low actor/system/read/write correctness is mostly NOT genuine agent extraction failure. The single biggest lever is a deterministic, explainable quote/quotation (+first-person actor) normalization, not an LLM judge or embeddings.
